newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares steady, t-bill market picks up.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares steady, t-bill market picks up.

text.p: Lithuanian shares were steady on Friday and dealers said that bearish markets across Eastern Europe were taking a bite out of the country's equity market.
"We forecast that prices will fall next week and then stabilize near the end of the week," said Arvydas Jacikevicius of brokerage house Suprema.
"The overall equities situation in Eastern Europe is not so good and this is having an impact here," he said.
The Baltic Ship yard was one of the session's few gainers, advancing to 9.97 litas from 9.07 litas.
Its prices has been buyoed by Denmark's Odense shipyard's acquisition of 43 percent of its shares in a block trade earlier this week.
The Danish company has promised to bring new investment and know-how to the shipyard, which employs 1,500 people and makes small ships, container feed ships and supply ships.
Ukio Bank was the most active listing on the banking sector in trade of almost 170,000 litas and its price advanced to 17.00 litas from 16.00 litas.
The dormant secondary T-bill market showed signs of life in trade of over six million litas but dealers said it was not the start of a long-term trend.
"One or two banks needed some cash to boost their liquidity," said one dealer.
Dealers hope that the market will pick up when the central bank begins repo auctions, which could start at the end of this month.
